content:
- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.3) or shows strong bearish momentum, model often underestimates downside risk; increase forecast downward buffer.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 1–2% of spike magnitude.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon (e.g., last 3 days negative), model often fails to adjust; force mean reversion toward recent 7-day average.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings; anchor forecast to 14-day moving average unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.3), model often exhibits lag; delay forecast adjustment until sentiment stabilizes or confirms direction.
